top_story.headline: Army's $50 billion MAPS professional-services contract adds a small-business-only teaming track
top_story.dek: Documents read today on the Army's Marketplace for Acquisition of Professional Services solicitation show a $50 billion ceiling, work in warzones and a new amendment that opens a separate track for small businesses.
paragraphs: The Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground is soliciting the Marketplace for Acquisition of Professional Services (MAPS), a multiple-award indefinite-delivery contract. According to Amendment 010, "The maximum total contract value (ceiling), including the Optional Ordering Period if exercised, is $50B." The statement of work says task-order locations "will be Government or contractor sites within CONUS and/or OCONUS locations, including warzone areas," and that some orders may require 24/7 operations, 365 days a year. These findings come from documents read today on a notice posted earlier. They are not a new notice.

The newest file is Amendment 0011, posted October 13. It states: "Only Small Businesses are permitted to submit SBTA proposals, subject to all terms and conditions outlined in this Solicitation." SBTA stands for small business teaming arrangement.

The question-and-answer spreadsheet posted April 24 shows how contested the terms have been. An industry question says Amendment 001, issued April 7, changed the recency requirement for qualifying projects from four years to three "without explanation." In its answers, the Army says a conditional Level 2 cybersecurity self-assessment is not acceptable and offerors must hold a final Level 2 certification. The Army also says its objective is to negotiate a fee "at a rate equal to or less than half the regulatory limits" in 10 U.S.C. 3322(b). A separate answer says a new Emerging Large Business category will be treated as large business after award.

sections.headline: Air Force asks industry for whitepapers to modernize its live-fire aircraft survivability test site
paragraphs: Two new solicitations were posted, and one was flagged. Documents read today on earlier notices also turned up three more items, listed below. The Army's $50 billion MAPS solicitation is covered in today's Top Story.

blocks.title: Air Force seeks whitepapers to modernize a live-fire test site at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base
blocks.text: The Arnold Engineering Development Complex, under the Air Force Test Center, is asking members of its AEDC Velocity Alliance Consortium and other industry partners for whitepapers. The project would modernize Test Site 2 at the Aerospace Vehicle Survivability Facility at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. The goal is a test facility able to safely and efficiently conduct live fire test and evaluation on current and future aerospace systems. The request uses Other Transaction Authority under 10 U.S.C. § 4022, which sits outside the standard federal contracting rules. The one attached file has not been read yet. A separate notice for the consortium itself is titled "Request for Whitepapers: AEDC Velocity Alliance - A Multi-Billion Dollar OTA Consortium Opportunity."

items: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation plans to buy two new IBM mainframes and five years of maintenance. According to the price schedule, the agency's current equipment "has reached end of life." (CORHQ-26-Q-0388)

Navy solicits high lift adapters, outriggers and push-up adapters, with optional yearly quantities for Australia's air force. The evaluation plan lists quantities of 0 to 10 for the Royal Australian Air Force alongside Navy quantities. (N6833526R1091)

Naval Research Laboratory seeks a senior research scientist for satellite radiation testing. The personnel document requires a Top Secret clearance with SCI credentials and at least 20 years of experience testing the effects of particle irradiation on satellite subsystems. (N0017326R0008)

blocks.text: Counts: 2 new, 0 repeats left out. The other new solicitation is a routine Veterans Affairs notice.

sections.headline: 232 new notices are almost all Defense Logistics Agency parts buys; an Army intelligence security-escort contract surfaced from a document
paragraphs: Of the 232 new combined synopsis/solicitations, 231 are Defense Logistics Agency parts buys that link to an outside portal (DIBBS) rather than to attachments on SAM.gov. None was flagged. A document read today on an earlier notice adds one item.

items: Army intelligence command seeks contractors for access control and security escorts at its classified facilities. The statement of work calls the services "essential contractor services" vital to the mobilization and national security mission of the Intelligence and Security Command's headquarters. It says they "must be maintained without interruption during crisis situations, natural disasters, civil disruptions, pandemics, or any other government closure or emergency activation." The file was posted September 23. (W50NH9-26-R-A028)

sections.headline: Army plans a Tripler Army Medical Center parking garage to close a 2,161-space shortfall
paragraphs: No new presolicitations were posted, and two were left out as repeats. Documents read today on notices posted earlier turned up three items, listed below.

items: Army's Honolulu engineer district plans a vehicle parking garage at Tripler Army Medical Center in Hawaii. An industry-day document says a parking study found "a substantial shortfall in parking capacity of 2,161 spaces" and that the project is needed to partially address it. (W9128A279A001)

blocks.text: Also read today: a Veterans Affairs plan for a five-year wheelchair transportation contract at the Charleston medical center (36C24726R0123) and a General Services Administration office lease in Forest, Mississippi (4MS0229). Counts: 0 new, 2 already reported and left out.

sections.headline: Army arsenal seeks automated cooling-water treatment for its gun-tube heat-treat furnace
paragraphs: No new special notices were posted. A document attached to an earlier notice is the only item.

items: Army's Watervliet Arsenal seeks automated chemical dosing to monitor and maintain cooling water for its Horizontal Gun Tube Heat Treat Furnace. The request falls under the arsenal's commercial solutions opening, and the file name gives a December 31, 2026 due date. (W911PT26SC001)

sections.headline: Veterans Affairs medical center restricts competition for a building automation upgrade to its current contractor, Conserv
paragraphs: No new Sources Sought notices were posted. Documents read today on earlier notices include two sole-source-style documents, shown below as cards. Both were posted under Sources Sought, not as justifications.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs medical center plans to give a building automation system upgrade to current contractor Conserv without competition
blocks.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs (Network Contract Office 10) notice for "6350--Upgrade Building Automation System" has a redacted "Restricting Competition" document attached. It says Conserv, Inc., the current maintenance contractor, "is the only firm capable of providing the services described above without the medical center experiencing substantial duplication of costs that could not be expected to be recovered through competition." The justification rests on equipment dependencies and facility outage constraints. The file was posted October 15.

blocks.title: Army plans a 9-month sole-source extension to wind down its neurocognitive testing program
blocks.text: The Department of the Army request for information for Neurocognitive Assessment Test Support Services quotes a planned modification for Controller Bay, LLC of Anchorage, Alaska. The modification would raise the contract's ceiling and extend its period of performance by 9 months. It cites the "only one responsible source" authority in 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). The document calls it "a limited, time-sensitive phase-out action required to support the orderly phase-out, transition of the program and final termination of the Army NCAT program."

items: Army asks industry about building hardened satellite communications terminals that can survive a high-altitude electromagnetic pulse. The request covers production, installation and sustainment support, and the government would install them with the supplier's technical support. (W15P7T-27-R-HMFT-R)

Special Operations Command Pacific looks for a vendor to lease up to twelve full-size SUVs on six-month terms in Hawaii. The draft statement of work says the vehicles are for rotational operational requirements, logistics movement and transit on Oahu. (H9228010152026)

Army seeks a contractor to maintain stormwater facilities at Joint Base Myer-Henderson Hall and Fort McNair. The notice says the facilities treat runoff from about 100 acres of Fort Myer-Henderson Hall. (W91QV127PA997)

paragraphs: There were 0 new awards of $2M+ (0 of them Defense Department awards just published after the 90-day hold), 2 large modifications and 0 cuts. Both modifications are Defense Department actions signed in July and only now published. Defense contract data is released with a 90-day delay. No routine items were screened out, so the end-of-edition list of other new awards is empty.

blocks.text: Lockheed Martin Corporation received a $219,222,018 modification from the Department of Defense (Department of the Army), signed July 17 and published this week. Modification PZ0005 is a definitized letter contract: an earlier letter contract that let work start before the price was settled now has final terms. The description says it covers fiscal 2025 M270A2 launchers (guided-missile launchers) and international spares. (award)

Electric Boat Corporation received a $149,028,497 modification from the Department of Defense (Department of the Navy), signed July 16 and published this week. Modification P00204 is a funding-only action, and its description says only "FUNDING ACTION." The classification codes point to shipbuilding work, but the record does not say which program. (award)
